note: Curation minutes per record, per PHASE, from record 25. Declared 2026-08-29 in F2, before a single record was timed, because nobody times a record twice: whatever this column does not carry on the day a record is curated, it never carries. F2_RULINGS.md rulings 46-48 carry the argument; this file is the data. ingest/cost.py holds the rules and ingest/cost_log.py is the only thing that writes here.
declared_on: 2026-08-29, F2, at commit 577a0e2, corpus 24 records, digest 26e4a683014bdf8a3dff98d48865a61869d137853333b82d024220c18eda9b28. The column is empty on purpose: F2 builds the instrument and F3 curates the first record it measures.
why_this_file_is_not_inside_the_records: Ruling 43's reason, unchanged and not expiring. ingest.loader.canonical_record_text hashes the whole parsed record with sorted keys, so a `minutes` key would change every content_hash and therefore corpus_digest -- the denominator of all 396 Block E runs and of the sonnet arm's 165. This is the SECOND file that would have moved it; the first was data/corpus_tiers.json, seven days ago.
why_it_is_not_under_data_seed_corpus: iter_seed_records REFUSES a .json at that depth: glob('*/*.json') would not see a file at the top level and rglob('*.json') would, and a file some walks see and others do not is the exact failure that function exists to prevent. data/corpus_tiers.json is the precedent; the ledger sits beside it.
why_ten: The tranche is 14 / 10 / 4 / 8 records per tier. Below ten, a per-tier mean moves further on one unusually hard record than on any change of method, so a trend line drawn through it would be a trend over noise with kill trigger 3 hanging off it. Declared NOW, at ten, with the consequence stated rather than discovered: published_translation_only (4 new) and catalogue_record (8 new) can NEVER be read as trends inside Block F, whatever their numbers do. Two of the four tiers that move can carry the claim. That is a fact about the block's size and it is cheaper to say here than at G3.
why_240: A clock started and left running overnight writes a working day of `measured` minutes into the one number kill trigger 3 depends on, and it arrives labelled as the most trustworthy kind of figure this file holds. Above four hours a span has to be closed as an explicit estimate with a written reason, which is a diff. Four hours rather than one, because a hard verbatim_with_provenance record genuinely can take an afternoon and a limit that fires on real work is a limit people route around.

phases.source_hunting: Finding a candidate source and deciding it is one. Searching institutional catalogues, corpora and scholarship; reading enough to know the text exists in a usable form; rejecting the ones that do not.
phases.rights_and_licence: Establishing that the text and any translation can be quoted and cited, and recording where that permission comes from. Counted separately from source_hunting because it is the phase most easily dropped without anyone noticing it has been.
phases.text_capture: Getting the source's own characters onto disk correctly: transcription or transfer, script and diacritics, normalisation, and checking the result against the page it came from.
phases.translation_and_fidelity: The English side and its honesty: locating or commissioning a translation, citing it, deciding the text_fidelity labels, and settling the record's tier.
phases.placement: W1 placement -- gazetteer lookup, ids, contested placements, or the written reason a record has none.
phases.authoring: Writing the record JSON, chunking it, and writing whatever gold cases it carries. Gold-case writing is inside curation and not beside it: a record curated without the case that tests it is a record the sweep cannot see.
phases.rework: Everything a failed check sent back: a red ingest.verify, a declared-vs-derived tier disagreement, a ranking regression traced to this record. Not a stage. It is the phase that tells you a tranche got faster by getting sloppier.

why_seven_phases: A single minutes figure per record is gameable by re-labelling work: cost trends down the moment source-hunting, rights checking, placement or gold-case writing stops being counted as curation. That is ruling 45's defect one level down -- an aggregate satisfied by changing what goes into it -- and the fix is the same shape. ingest/cost.py refuses a record entry that omits a phase, so a phase that went to zero has to SAY zero and the fall lands in the phase that stopped rather than in a total nobody can decompose.

comparator.declared_on: 2026-08-29, F2, before the first number. Ruling 46.
comparator.what_it_means: Kill trigger 3 is evaluated as a trend across records 25 to 60, per tier, in curation order -- and as nothing else. The claim available to G3 is 'within the 36 records Block F curated, cost per record in tier T moved thus', with n stated beside it.
comparator.why_not_record_12: Because nothing anywhere records what record 12 cost. The seed 24 were curated before any column existed; there is no minutes figure for any of them and none can be reconstructed. The trigger as written -- 'if record 60 costs what record 12 cost, 200 is a staffing question rather than an engineering one' -- therefore cannot be evaluated, and saying so in advance is the whole of ruling 46. A comparator chosen after the numbers are in is a comparator fitted to them.
comparator.what_was_considered_and_refused: Re-timing three or four seed records now to manufacture a baseline. Refused: re-curating a solved record measures re-doing it -- sources already found, rights already cleared, placement already decided -- so it is systematically cheap and would bias the trigger toward 'costs have not fallen'. A reconstructed estimate was refused for ruling 39's reason.
comparator.the_weaker_claim_stated_plainly: Within-tranche is a DIFFERENT and WEAKER claim than the trigger as written. It cannot tell you whether the machine got cheaper than it was at record 12; it can only tell you whether it got cheaper across the 36 records that came after 24. G3 reports it as that, or it reports nothing.
comparator.n_note: New records per tier, from data/corpus_tiers.json target_mix.by_tier_new. A trend over eight catalogue records is not a measurement anyone should stake 200 on, and min_n_to_read_as_a_trend is what stops the report drawing one.

The hunt these minutes measured moved off Kedukan Bukit and onto C. 87. Wikipedia's English translation of Kedukan Bukit is UNATTRIBUTED -- the article names Coedes 1930 and de Casparis 1975 in its bibliography but does not say whose English it prints -- and verbatim_with_provenance requires a published translation that is CITED. Attributing an anonymous translation would have put a name in translation_source that no page supports. The Campa corpus carries C. 87 with an English translation, a named editor and an explicit CC BY 3.0 licence, so the record that lands is seasia-05-my-son-b6.

Talang Tuo's English translation IS attributed -- to Coedes -- so it is verbatim_with_provenance material, and Southeast Asia's two vwp slots are already filled by records 25 and 26. check_delivery would refuse it as over-delivery. These minutes measured a hunt for a verbatim_machine_english record and found, across six candidates, that Southeast Asia's published epigraphy does not contain one: see the finding recorded in PROGRESS.md.

source_hunting.because: RECONSTRUCTED, not clocked, and the reason it was not clocked is the point: this hunt produced NO record, so there was no record id to start a clock against. F4. The clock was started on Silko's text_capture and the Greek was captured, and then the record's ORDER changed rather than its status: Monumentum Adulitanum II was curated first because its published English is readable at tertullian.org, while Silko's is Fontes Historiae Nubiorum III p. 1147, a free 54 MB PDF that costs a human pass. Silko WILL exist -- it is F4's second Sub-Saharan Africa verbatim_with_provenance record and ruling 58 names it -- so this is not FINDING 38's hunt-that-landed-nothing. Retired because ingest.verify refuses a ledger row whose record is not in the corpus, and that refusal is correct: a row for a record that is coming is indistinguishable from a row for a record that never will. The 1.7 measured minutes are re-filed on Silko with add when it lands, which writes them as estimated -- ruling 52's deliberate cost, paid here for an ordering decision rather than for a change of subject.
retired.reinstated_because: RULING 59, F4. This row was retired legitimately at 17:2x UTC, when africa-04-silko-talmis was not in the corpus: Monumentum Adulitanum II was curated first because its published English was readable, while Silko's took four more hours and three failed routes to reach. The record landed at 18:0x UTC and the retirement became illegal the moment it did -- ruling 52 writes its anti-loophole as a permanent property of the ledger and retirement as an event, and the two disagree exactly here. The minutes were already re-filed on this record as estimated. The retired row is kept with both dates and both reasons, because ruling 52's own sentence is that excluding by a recorded rule is a diff, and this is the diff that says the exclusion ended.

retirement.declared_on: 2026-08-31, F3, on the first record this project ever timed. Ruling 52.
retirement.what_it_is: A row whose record will NEVER EXIST, moved out of `records` and kept with the date and the written reason it was retired. It is not a delete. Every minute it recorded is still on disk and still readable.
retirement.why_it_was_needed: Source hunting is the phase that DECIDES which record exists, so the clock cannot be started against the right record id until the phase it is timing is over. The first record proved it in under three minutes: the clock was opened on seasia-04-vo-canh, the hunt then ruled that source out, and ingest.verify went red on a stale row the CLI had no way to correct. F2 predicted exactly this -- 'the FIRST record F3 curates is the first test of the CLI under real conditions'.
retirement.the_anti_loophole: A row may be retired ONLY if its record is not in the corpus. Without that clause, `retire` is a way to take the expensive records out of the column kill trigger 3 reads. This is floor.json's a_named_sweep_must_actually_fail_the_rule one file over: a list that can hold a qualifying row is a place to put numbers nobody liked.
retirement.what_happens_to_the_minutes: They are NOT carried across automatically, and that is the ruling rather than an omission. A span measured against a record id the hunt had not yet settled is not a measurement of the record that landed. It is re-filed with `add`, which writes ESTIMATED and demands a written reason -- ruling 48, where the weaker provenance wins.
retirement.why_kept_rather_than_deleted: Excluding by a recorded rule is a diff. Excluding by making a row vanish is not, and is forbidden here for the reason floor.json gives about moving sweep files out of the way.

why_agent: FINDING 70, F5 Part 3, closed in F6 on 2026-09-06 in the shape that finding asked for: 'An `agent` field per phase, or per record, is the obvious shape and this session did not add one ... F6's, with the evidence already in the file.' PER PHASE and not per record, because records 37 to 40 cannot be described by one value: one phase of seven is the curator's own self-reported minutes and five are model wall clock apportioned across phases by judgement. A per-record field would have to choose, and the flattering choice is the one nobody would check. THE TEETH ARE IN THE REPORT, NOT IN A GATE: ingest.cost.trend_line REFUSES to print a first-half/second-half trend for any tier whose minutes come from more than one agent, however far above min_n_to_read_as_a_trend it sits -- which is the risk FINDING 70 actually names, that verbatim_with_provenance is 'about to be read as a trend by somebody who does not know that four of its timed entries measure a different agent'. n is the wrong guard for that: being above the floor is what makes it dangerous. `unrecorded` is a VALUE and not an absence, and entries curated on or after 2026-09-06 may not use it.
